thread:
alex: Hey team — customer AcmeApp reporting streaming truncation in Safari when going through their CDN. They see full chunks for ~8–12s then the client stops receiving anything and never reconnects automatically. Happens for chat streaming only, not for short non-stream requests. Repro steps from them pasted below.

alex: Repro (from customer):
1) Client: Safari 15.6 on macOS 12.4 using native EventSource.
2) Connect to our hosted SSE endpoint: https://api.redwood.test/v1/stream?model=gpt-open.
3) They get some partial data lines then server stops pushing and connection shows as closed in the browser devtools with a 304 on a subsequent /edge/check request.

alex: They say the problem goes away if they bypass CDN (request straight to origin) or if they use Chrome. Also they said adding a random query param every request seems to avoid it (so maybe cache).

maria: Can you paste the raw request/response headers from their failing trace? especially Cache-Control and any 304 responses?

alex: Yep, from their capture:

Request: GET /v1/stream?session=abc HTTP/1.1
Host: cdn.acme.example
Authorization: Bearer <token redacted>
Accept: text/event-stream
Cache-Control: no-cache
Connection: keep-alive

Edge response (first chunk, 200):
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, stale-while-revalidate=60
Vary: Accept-Encoding
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

data: {"delta":"Hello"}

Edge subsequent probe (304):
GET /edge/check HTTP/1.1
-> 304 Not Modified

alex: Browser devtools shows EventSource reported closed after the 304 and then no automatic reconnect.

jen (support): Interesting. Do they use any EventSource polyfill? Safari sometimes has different reconnect heuristics. Also if the CDN is returning 304 for some side-request that the client relies on, could be killing keep-alive?

emily: @alex can you confirm whether the Acme CDN strips or modifies the `Connection` header? Cloud/CDN edges sometimes terminate keep-alive, and if they return 304 for a conditional request, some browsers treat that as end-of-stream if there are missing SSE terminators.

alex: Customer says no polyfills, native `EventSource`. They tested with `fetch`-based chunked polyfill and it worked (kept re-requesting and resumed), so that hints at EventSource behavior in Safari with 304s.

sanjay: @maria @emily could this be our service issuing a conditional validation on an edge health/keepalive causing the 304? We don't usually return 304 for SSE endpoints. Any edge rewrite?

eng-runtime-bot: Note: recent deploy (2026-12-01) included an optimization to set `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, stale-while-revalidate=60` on streaming endpoints behind CDN for bandwidth reasons.

maria: Whoa — we shouldn't have a `public` caching header on streaming endpoints. That may cause CDN to try to cache and issue conditional requests. SSE must be passed through as uncacheable or with `Cache-Control: no-transform, no-store` depending on the CDN to avoid rewriting.

alex: The customer claims bypassing CDN resolves it. So likely CDN is caching/conditionalizing and returning 304 for some non-idempotent long-poll stream, then Safari's `EventSource` sees that and closes the connection. Chrome may be more forgiving.

jen (support): Action items for triage:
- Acquire a pcap / full HAR from customer to confirm 304 timing.
- Reproduce with `curl -v` against CDN and origin.
- Try toggling cache headers from origin to confirm behavior.

alex: I asked them for HAR. Meanwhile I tried a quick `curl` from my mac against our sandbox behind the same CDN:

curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://sandbox-redwood.cdn.test/v1/stream?model=test
* Connected to sandbox-redwood.cdn.test (1.2.3.4) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/stream?model=test HTTP/1.1
> Host: sandbox-redwood.cdn.test
> Accept: text/event-stream
>
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
< cache-control: public, max-age=0, stale-while-revalidate=60
< transfer-encoding: chunked

data: {"delta":"hi"}

# then after ~10s the edge issues a 304 on a separate conditional probe
* Received HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified for /edge/check
* Connection #0 to host sandbox-redwood.cdn.test left intact

alex: Curl left the TCP connection open (didn't close). But Safari's EventSource still stops receiving. So maybe EventSource layer expects some keep-alive framing and doesn't resume on a 304 timing. Our curl test isn't an exact match.

sanjay: We should check whether the CDN is returning a `Content-Length: 0` or `Connection: close` on that probe. That could be interpreted poorly by Safari. Also check for stray `Content-Encoding` changes.

maria: Proposed mitigation: roll back the deploy change that added `public, max-age=0` on streaming endpoints. Immediately set `Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, private` on SSE endpoints until we have a proper CDN passthrough rule. Can someone on eng-runtime cut a quick config? @sanjay? :pray:

sanjay: I can push a config to mark `/v1/stream*` endpoints as `Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-transform` at the origin for now. Doing it in the next 10 mins.

deploy-bot: Deploy started by sanjay: origin-configs/patch-312 -> staging -> prod (rolling)

eng-runtime-bot: Rollout NOTE: change touches header middleware for websocket/sse routing. Canary to 10% first.

alex: Customer just uploaded HAR — attaching key excerpt here:

# HAR excerpt
{"request":{"url":"https://cdn.acme.example/v1/stream?session=abc","headers":[{"name":"Accept","value":"text/event-stream"}]},"response":{"status":200,"headers":[{"name":"Cache-Control","value":"public, max-age=0, stale-while-revalidate=60"}]},"entries":[{"time":11500,"response":{"status":304,"statusText":"Not Modified","headers":[{"name":"Date","value":"..."}]}}]}

jen (support): Good. Once the header rollback lands, can you ask them to test by making a fresh connection (no param) and also to test Safari with a disabled cache (devtools) to see if behavior changes?

emily: Also ask them to test using an EventSource polyfill (fetch-based) as temporary workaround — you mentioned that earlier. If fetch polyfill works but native fails, it's definitely client parsing/heuristics. Polyfill may be a viable short-term patch.

maria: Long-term we should add an automated test: run Safari headless + synthetic CDN that issues conditional 304s during long-lived streams to replicate this. I can put a ticket.

sanjay: Update: patch rolled to prod canary 10% — headers updated for SSE endpoints to `Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-transform` at origin. Monitoring logs for 5 minutes.

eng-runtime-bot: Canary metrics: no increase in error-rate so far. Latency stable.

alex: I sent the customer a note: asked them to test now and provided two mitigations: (1) temporary EventSource polyfill, (2) confirm after we pushed header change. I'll update this thread when they confirm. :thumbsup:

jen (support): Thanks Alex. Keep me posted — if they escalate to enterprise SLA we'll need a bridge.

alex: Customer replied: quick test — Safari still saw truncation when loading via CDN, but when they disabled cache in devtools, stream stayed live as expected. So the header change might help but they're still seeing odd behavior. They also said the CDN is inserting a `304` on a collateral probe to `/edge/check` with `Connection: close` which may prompt Safari to treat the TCP connection as broken even if SSE channel remains — we need to verify that behavior across browsers.

maria: Next steps: (1) get the CDN vendor team to confirm probe behavior (does their probe close TCP or just 304?), (2) instrument origin to emit a small keep-alive comment (`: keepalive\n\n`) every 15s so browsers don't time out, (3) add an SSE-specific passthrough CDN rule so edges don't cache or probe these endpoints.

sanjay: I'll open a vendor ticket and add keepalive ping header logic to runtime within the hour. Will report back with ticket ID.

alex: Thanks all — I'll keep triage and coordinate with customer. Will update thread once CDN vendor responds or if we get a repro in our staging harness.

emily: Filing internal DEEP ticket: SSE-304-SAFARI-CACHE to track.

jen (support): Great. If anything changes on customer side, post here. :eyes:
